questions.topic: Heat capacity graph and temperature rise
concepts: heat capacity graph and temperature rise
questions.question: For three different substances P, Q and R, the graph of heat capacity versus mass is shown (straight lines through the origin; P steepest, Q intermediate, R least steep). Then which of the three substances will show rapid rise in temperature when equal amount of heat is supplied?
questions.solution: (c) R. Slope of heat capacity vs mass = specific heat capacity; R has the least specific heat capacity, so for the same mass and heat it shows the greatest (most rapid) rise in temperature (Δθ = Q/mc).

questions.question:
Match the following:
Source while in use: 1. Sun  2. Thermocouple  3. Dynamo  4. Photocell
Energy conversion: (P) Mechanical to Electrical  (Q) Light to Electrical  (R) Heat to Electrical  (S) Light to Chemical
questions.solution: (c) 1-S, 2-R, 3-P, 4-Q. Sun - light to chemical (photosynthesis); thermocouple - heat to electrical; dynamo - mechanical to electrical; photocell - light to electrical.

questions.question: A bar magnet (N pole facing coil AB, S pole facing coil CD) is kept between two coils AB and CD, each connected to a galvanometer. Two magnetic needles N and N' are kept near the outer ends A and D of the two coils respectively. If the magnet is moved towards the right side, identify the correct positions (directions of the north end) of the magnetic needles.

options.a: N points right (→), N' points left (←)
options.b: N points left (←), N' points right (→)
options.c: N points left (←), N' points left (←)
options.d: N points right (→), N' points right (→)

questions.solution: (b) N points left (←), N' points right (→). Magnet moves away from AB (N pole receding), so end B becomes S to attract it and end A becomes N: needle N near A points away from A, i.e. left. S pole approaches C, so C becomes S to repel it and D becomes N: needle N' near D points away from D, i.e. right.
questions.figure_desc: Two coils AB (left) and CD (right) each with a galvanometer; bar magnet N-S between them moving right; compass needles N (left of A) and N' (right of D) initially pointing north; four option pairs of needle directions.

questions.question: In beta emission, the daughter element is an ............ of the parent atom.
questions.solution: (b) isobar. Mass number is unchanged and atomic number increases by 1, so the daughter is an isobar.

questions.question: If 200 V is applied to the primary coil of an ideal step-up transformer with turns ratio 5, then the voltage in the secondary coil is:

Assertion (A): It is advisable to transmit electric power at a high voltage.
Reason (R): High voltage implies high current can transmit electric power easily over a long distance.

options.a: Both A and R are true, R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true and R is false
options.d: A is false and R is true

questions.solution: (c) A is true and R is false. A is true. R is false: for the same power, high voltage means LOW current, which reduces I²R heating loss in the line wires.

questions.topic: EMF, terminal voltage and internal resistance
concepts: emf, terminal voltage and internal resistance
questions.question: For a given cell (e.m.f. ε, internal resistance r) connected to an external resistance R, if e.m.f. is twice its terminal voltage, then which of the following relations is true?
questions.solution: (a) R = r. ε = I(R + r) and V = IR; ε = 2V ⇒ R + r = 2R ⇒ R = r.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
questions.solution: (c) Human jaw (biting) - Class III. Scissors are class I, wheelbarrow and nutcracker are class II; the human jaw while biting is a class III lever.

questions.question: An opera singer sings a very high-pitched note and causes a glass to shatter. Which of the following is the correct reason for the glass to shatter?

options.a: The amplitude of the sound is very large
options.b: The frequency of the sound is high
options.d: The quality of sound is high

questions.solution: (c) Due to resonance. The note's frequency matches the natural frequency of the glass, so it vibrates with very large amplitude (resonance) and breaks.

questions.question: The electromagnetic radiation which is useful in night photography is:
questions.solution: (a) infra-red rays. Infrared rays are less scattered (penetrate haze) and are emitted by warm objects, so they are used for night/haze photography.

questions.topic: Refraction of colours through glass slab
concepts: refraction of colours through glass slab
questions.question: Three monochromatic light rays are incident on a glass slab at the same angle of incidence one by one. If the three incident rays are of colours yellow, blue and green respectively, identify the colours of the emergent rays in order. (In the figure, inside the slab ray A is bent most towards the normal and emerges with the greatest lateral displacement, C the least; all emergent rays are parallel to the incident ray.)

options.a: A - Blue, B - Green, C - Yellow
options.b: A - Blue, B - Yellow, C - Green
options.c: A - Yellow, B - Blue, C - Green
options.d: A - Yellow, B - Green, C - Blue

questions.solution: (a) A - Blue, B - Green, C - Yellow. Refractive index of glass is greatest for blue, then green, then yellow; so blue bends most towards the normal and is displaced most (A), green next (B), yellow least (C).

questions.question: Which of the following lenses would you prefer to use while reading small letters found in a dictionary?

options.a: A convex lens of focal length 50 cm
options.b: A concave lens of focal length 50 cm
options.c: A convex lens of focal length 5 cm
options.d: A concave lens of focal length 5 cm

questions.solution: (c) A convex lens of focal length 5 cm. A convex lens of short focal length acts as a magnifying glass giving a large, erect, virtual image.

questions.question: Write any two common properties of electromagnetic waves.
questions.solution: Any two: (1) they travel in vacuum with the same speed 3 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹; (2) they are transverse waves (oscillating electric and magnetic fields perpendicular to each other and to the direction of travel); (3) they do not need a material medium; (4) they are not deflected by electric or magnetic fields; (5) they show reflection, refraction, interference.

questions.topic: Position of centre of gravity using moments
concepts: position of centre of gravity using moments
questions.question:
A stick is balanced on a point (pivot) and is kept horizontal by a force of 30 N hanging from end A at a distance of 0.35 m from the pivot. The weight of the stick is greater than 30 N.
(a) Copy the diagram and mark the probable position of the C.G. of the stick as G.
(b) If the fulcrum moves towards the C.G., then in which direction will the stick turn?
questions.solution: (a) G lies on the other side of the pivot from A, at a distance less than 0.35 m from the pivot (W × x = 30 × 0.35 = 10.5 N m with W > 30 N ⇒ x < 0.35 m). (b) The moment of the weight decreases and the moment of the 30 N force increases, so the stick turns anticlockwise - end A moves down.

marking_points.point: (a) G marked on the side opposite to A, closer to the pivot than 0.35 m
(b) Turns anticlockwise / end A goes down

questions.figure_desc: A horizontal stick on a triangular pivot with a 30 N force hanging downward at the left end A; the longer part of the stick lies to the right of the pivot.

questions.topic: Power of an engine lifting coal
concepts: power of an engine lifting coal
questions.question: Find the power of an engine in kW required to lift 10⁵ kg of coal per hour from a mine 360 m deep. (Take g = 10 m s⁻²)
Give reason: The vessel used for measurement of heat (calorimeter) is made of a thin sheet of copper.
questions.solution: Copper has a low specific heat capacity and a thin sheet has small mass, so the calorimeter has a low heat capacity and absorbs very little heat from its contents. Copper is also a good conductor, so it quickly attains the temperature of its contents.

marking_points.point: Low specific heat capacity / thin so small heat capacity - absorbs little heat
Good conductor - quickly attains temperature of contents

questions.question: Two beakers A and B contain the same liquid, heated to two different temperatures: A at 20°C and B at 100°C. If a ray of light enters from air into the liquid in both the beakers, then in which beaker does the light ray bend more? Justify your answer.
questions.solution: In beaker A (20°C). Refractive index of a liquid decreases with increase in temperature (the liquid becomes less dense and light travels faster in it), so the cooler liquid in A has a higher refractive index and bends the ray more towards the normal.

marking_points.point: Refractive index decreases as temperature increases

questions.topic: Torque on a wheel from forces at angles
concepts: torque on a wheel from forces at angles
questions.question:
A wheel of radius 20 cm is pivoted at its centre O. Forces act on the rim: 4 N at A tangentially (at 90° to OA); 8 N at B at an angle of 30° to the radius BO; 6 N at C directed along the radius towards O; 9 N at D tangentially (at 90° to OD). Then:
(a) Which of the given forces will produce maximum torque about O?
(b) Calculate the torque produced by force 8 N about O.
questions.solution: Torque = F × perpendicular distance. 4 N: 4 × 0.2 = 0.8 N m; 8 N: 8 × 0.2 × sin 30° = 0.8 N m; 6 N: acts through O, torque 0; 9 N: 9 × 0.2 = 1.8 N m. (a) The 9 N force produces the maximum torque (1.8 N m). (b) Torque of 8 N = 8 × 0.2 × sin 30° = 8 × 0.1 = 0.8 N m.
questions.figure_desc: Wheel of radius 20 cm centred at O with 4 N tangential at A (top), 8 N at B (left) at 30° to the horizontal radius, 6 N at C (bottom) pointing up along the radius, 9 N tangential downward at D (right).

concepts: factors affecting internal resistance of a cell
questions.question:
Figure A shows an electric cell (two electrodes dipped in electrolyte connected through R) and figures B and C show some changes made in the original cell A: in B the electrodes are placed closer together; in C the electrodes are of larger area (wider plates).
(a) Which factor will be affected by the changes made to the cell in figure A?
(b) How do the changes made in figures B and C affect the factor stated by you?
questions.solution: (a) The internal resistance of the cell. (b) Figure B: decreasing the separation between the electrodes decreases the internal resistance. Figure C: increasing the area of the electrodes (in the electrolyte) decreases the internal resistance.

marking_points.point: (b) B: electrodes closer - internal resistance decreases
(b) C: larger electrode area - internal resistance decreases

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
A vibrating tuning fork is placed over the mouth of a burette filled with water. The tap is opened and the water level gradually falls. It is observed that sound becomes the loudest for a particular length of the air column.
(a) What is the name of the phenomenon taking place when this happens?
(b) Why does the sound become the loudest?
(c) What is the name of the phenomenon taking place when sound is produced for another length of air column and is not the loudest?
(d) If the water level in the burette falls further, will you notice the same observation again?
questions.solution: (a) Resonance. (b) At this length the natural frequency of the air column equals the frequency of the tuning fork, so the air column vibrates with maximum amplitude, giving the loudest sound. (c) Forced vibrations. (d) Yes - resonance occurs again at a longer air column (about three times the first resonating length), though the sound is slightly fainter.

marking_points.point: (b) Natural frequency of air column equals frequency of fork - maximum amplitude
(d) Yes, at a longer length (≈3 times)

questions.question: A piece of ice at −20°C is heated at a constant rate and its temperature recorded at regular intervals till 100°C. Draw a temperature-time graph to represent the change in phase. Label the different parts of your graph.
questions.solution: Temperature on y-axis, time on x-axis: (1) AB - steep rise from −20°C to 0°C (ice heating; ice has lower specific heat capacity, so steeper); (2) BC - horizontal at 0°C (melting: ice + water, latent heat of fusion absorbed); (3) CD - rise from 0°C to 100°C (water heating, less steep); (4) DE - horizontal at 100°C (boiling: water + steam, latent heat of vaporisation; longer plateau).

questions.topic: Semiconductor resistivity; materials for standard resistors
concepts: semiconductor resistivity; materials for standard resistors
questions.question:
(a) How does the specific resistance of a semiconductor change with the increase in temperature?
(b) Name the materials which are used for making standard resistors. Give reason to support your answer.
questions.solution: (a) It decreases with increase in temperature. (b) Alloys such as manganin and constantan (eureka). Their resistivity is high and changes very little with temperature (very low temperature coefficient of resistance), so the resistance stays constant.

marking_points.point: (b) Resistance almost unaffected by temperature (and high resistivity)

questions.topic: Power of heater to melt ice with efficiency
concepts: power of heater to melt ice with efficiency
questions.question: Calculate the power of an electric heater required to melt 1 kg of ice at 0°C in 30 s if the efficiency of the heater is 40%. Specific latent heat of ice = 336 J g⁻¹.
questions.solution: Heat needed = mL = 1000 × 336 = 336000 J. Useful power = 336000/30 = 11200 W. Efficiency 40% ⇒ input power = 11200/0.4 = 28000 W = 28 kW.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Transformer: principle, d.c. input, laminated core
concepts: transformer: principle, d.c. input, laminated core
questions.question:
Study the picture (a laminated soft iron core with an input coil connected to an a.c. input voltage and an output coil giving a larger a.c. output voltage) and answer the questions:
(a) Identify the electric device shown in the picture.
(b) Name the principle on which this device works.
(c) If the a.c. input is replaced by d.c., then what will be the impact on the output voltage? Give reason to support your answer.
(d) Why is the soft iron core used in this device laminated?
questions.solution: (a) A transformer (step-up transformer, as the output voltage is larger). (b) Electromagnetic induction (mutual induction). (c) There will be no output voltage (except a momentary one when switched on/off), because d.c. produces a constant magnetic flux; no change in flux means no induced e.m.f. in the secondary. (d) Laminations reduce eddy currents in the core and hence reduce energy loss as heat.

marking_points.point: (c) Output zero - no change in flux with d.c.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Relation between initial speed and maximum height
concepts: relation between initial speed and maximum height
questions.question:
A body of mass m is thrown vertically upward under gravity with some initial velocity u. After some time interval t, the body reaches its maximum height h and falls back to the ground. Then:
(a) How are the quantities u and h related to each other?
(b) What assumption have you made in part (a)?
questions.solution: (a) By conservation of energy, ½mu² = mgh ⇒ h = u²/2g (u² = 2gh; h ∝ u²). (b) Air resistance (friction) is neglected, i.e. mechanical energy is conserved (and g is constant).

questions.question:
A wave has a wavelength 10⁻³ nm.
(a) Name the wave.
(b) State its one property different from other electromagnetic waves.
(c) State its one use.
questions.solution: (a) Gamma (γ) rays (λ = 10⁻¹² m). (b) Highest frequency/energy and highest penetrating power of all e.m. waves; emitted from the nucleus of radioactive atoms. (c) To kill cancer cells (radiotherapy) / sterilise medical equipment / preserve food.

marking_points.point: (b) Highest penetrating power / energy / from nucleus

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
A cell of e.m.f. 1.5 V and internal resistance 1 Ω is connected to resistors of 4 Ω and 10 Ω in series. Calculate:
(a) the current through the 10 Ω resistor.
(b) the voltage drop across the cell when the current is flowing.
(c) the terminal voltage.
questions.solution: (a) I = ε/(R + r) = 1.5/(4 + 10 + 1) = 0.1 A (same in series, so 0.1 A through 10 Ω). (b) Voltage drop (lost volts) inside the cell = Ir = 0.1 × 1 = 0.1 V. (c) Terminal voltage V = ε − Ir = 1.5 − 0.1 = 1.4 V (= 0.1 × 14).

questions.question:
The circuit diagram shows dual control switches S1 and S2 (each with terminals a, b, c) for a staircase electric light, in the OFF condition. Copy the diagram and show the circuit in the ON condition when
(a) switch S1 is operated
(b) switch S2 is operated
(c) Identify and write the error in the given diagram.
questions.solution: (a) S1 is changed from a-b to b-c: current path L → bulb → S1 (b-c) → wire c-c → S2 (c-b) → N; the bulb glows. (b) Starting from the off position, S2 is changed from b-c to b-a: path L → bulb → S1 (b-a) → wire a-a → S2 (a-b) → N; the bulb glows. (c) Error: the bulb is connected directly to the live wire and the switches (and the fuse) are in the neutral wire; the switches (and fuse) should be connected in the live wire.

(b) S2 switched to b-a showing closed path

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: An object of height 4 cm is placed at a distance 24 cm in front of a convex lens of focal length 8 cm. Find the position and the size of the image.
questions.solution: u = −24 cm, f = +8 cm. 1/v = 1/f + 1/u = 1/8 − 1/24 = 2/24 ⇒ v = +12 cm (real, on the other side). m = v/u = 12/(−24) = −0.5 ⇒ image height = −0.5 × 4 = −2 cm, i.e. 2 cm tall, inverted.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Balancing a fission equation; chain reaction
concepts: balancing a fission equation; chain reaction
questions.question:
(a) Copy and complete the following nuclear fission reaction:
²³⁵₉₂U + ¹₀n → ....₅₇La + ⁸⁵....Br + ....¹₀n + energy
(b) What is another name given to nuclear fission? Give a reason.
questions.solution: (a) ²³⁵₉₂U + ¹₀n → ¹⁴⁸₅₇La + ⁸⁵₃₅Br + 3 ¹₀n + energy. (Atomic numbers: 92 = 57 + 35; mass numbers: 236 = 148 + 85 + 3.) (b) It is called a (nuclear) chain reaction, because the neutrons released in one fission go on to cause fission of more uranium nuclei, so the reaction becomes self-sustaining. (Also known as "splitting of the nucleus".)

marking_points.point: (a) Mass number of La = 148 and atomic number of Br = 35

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Speed of sound by repeated echo
concepts: speed of sound by repeated echo
questions.question: A boy stands 102 m in front of a wall and claps. The boy continues to clap every time an echo is heard. Another boy finds that the time between the first and the thirty-first clap is 18 s. Calculate the speed of sound in the air.
questions.solution: Between the 1st and 31st clap there are 30 intervals, so time for one echo t = 18/30 = 0.6 s. v = 2d/t = (2 × 102)/0.6 = 340 m s⁻¹.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Lever combined with block and tackle
concepts: lever combined with block and tackle
questions.question: The diagram shows a combination of a block and tackle system of pulleys (2 pulleys in the upper fixed block, 2 pulleys in the lower movable block, string tied to the upper block, so 4 segments support the lower block) with a lever AB: the fulcrum F is 70 cm from end A and 30 cm from end B; the free end of the pulley string is attached to B and effort E is applied upward at A. If the efficiency of the block and tackle system is 90% and the weight of the metallic block is 72 N, calculate the effort E required at end A to lift the metallic block.
questions.solution: Block and tackle: VR = 4 (four strands support the lower block). MA = η × VR = 0.9 × 4 = 3.6. Force needed at B (string tension) = L/MA = 72/3.6 = 20 N. Lever: E × 70 = 20 × 30 ⇒ E = 600/70 ≈ 8.57 N.
questions.figure_desc: Lever AB with fulcrum F (70 cm to A, 30 cm to B), upward effort E at A; string from B goes over a block and tackle with two pulleys in each block supporting a metallic block.

questions.question:
The figure shows the section of a semi-circular glass slab having its centre at O. Three rays of light A, B and C of the same colour are incident on the curved surface (along radii) and strike the edge XY at the point O. The light ray B suffers refraction along OB' (grazing along XY). Ray A makes a smaller angle with the normal at O than B, and ray C a larger angle.
(a) Copy the diagram and show the critical angle by C'.
(b) Draw the path of rays A and C after they strike the edge XY.
(c) Name the phenomenon which ray C exhibits.
questions.solution: (a) Draw the normal at O (perpendicular to XY); the angle between ray B (inside the glass) and this normal is the critical angle C'. (b) Ray A (angle of incidence < C') refracts out into air at O, bending away from the normal. Ray C (angle of incidence > C') is totally internally reflected at O back into the glass, with angle of reflection = angle of incidence, and leaves through the curved surface undeviated (along a radius). (c) Total internal reflection.

marking_points.point: (a) Critical angle C' marked between ray B and the normal at O
(b) Ray A refracted into air away from the normal
(b) Ray C totally reflected back into glass, angle r = angle i
